nodes.title: Game mix-up naming in stambh/tally, kon/place and kon/name runs in shadow: the rules as built write wouldName to the trail and trace, and nothing reaches the teacher's row, the seam or the learner model. No further judge reads a battery; real sittings decide: a mode is switched on with at least 30 shadow namings and at most 1 in 10 contradicted by the lesson's verified-key classification. Before shadow: the three 'blocks' fixes (Yahi naam waits until the name changes; tally read's discriminating row; draw wrong-scale against last level's right mark) and the judges' children added to the battery. New play law for every family: after a miss the check control waits until her act changes. Reverse: more than 3 in 10 contradicted after 30 namings drops repeat naming for that mode.

Gate 2 second reading at integration 72 (46782fd15): three Opus judges, one per mode, each ran the battery (full sweep passes, tables reproduced) and wrote new children against the served path. All FAIL. stambh/tally: discriminating level not built for numbers (rows 25, 31, 37, 43, 49 counted for 'a bundle skipped'); worst single-habit non-holder 0.013; two habits at once 0.25. kon/place: draw wrong-scale has no discriminating check ('last time's right dot' 0.075, counted pair found); a finger inside the angle 0.075. kon/name: an unchanged second press of Yahi naam confirms (careful child with two slips 0.98; blind guesser 0.13); same swap then random letters 0.13; then another order of the same letters 0.84. Holders: vertex-off 0.92 to 0.93, other scale 1.00, vertex first/last 1.00, tally read 0.80, always inner 0.

Two readings of gate 2 had the same shape: a proof over children we listed, and a judge who listed more (first habits, then acts shared with the mix-up on some level and behaviours after a miss). Each repair held and each reading found the next list, because every child in the proof is one someone imagined. A line set against imagined children cannot close; what a child does after a miss has to be measured on real sittings.
